questions.question: By interchanging the given two signs and numbers which of the following equation will be not correct? + and ×, 5 and 4 I. 4 + 8 × 5 – 7 ÷ 1 = 37 II. 5 × 3 – 4 + 6 ÷ 2 = –8
questions.questionHtml:
By interchanging the given two signs and numbers which of the following equation will be not correct?

+ and ×, 5 and 4

I. 4 + 8 × 5 – 7 ÷ 1 = 37

II. 5 × 3 – 4 + 6 ÷ 2 = –8
questions.solution:
I. 4 + 8 × 5 – 7 ÷ 1 = 37

After interchanging the signs + and ×, and numbers, 5 and 4 in the given equation, we have

5 × 8 + 4 – 7 ÷ 1 = 37

Applying BODMAS Rule, we get

5 × 8 + 4 – 7 = 37

⇒ 40 + 4 – 7 = 37

⇒ 44 - 7 = 37

⇒ 37 = 37

The given equation is correct.

II. 5 × 3 – 4 + 6 ÷ 2 = –8

After interchanging the signs + and ×, and numbers, 5 and 4 in the given equation, we have

4 + 3 – 5 × 6 ÷ 2 = –8

Applying BODMAS Rule, we get

4 + 3 – 5 × 3 = –8

⇒ 4 + 3 – 15 = –8

⇒ 7 – 15 = –8

⇒ -8 = –8

The given equation is correct.

Hence, "Neither I nor II" is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which two signs and two numbers should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct? 60 × 3 + 660 ÷ 6 – 20 = 290
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs and two numbers should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct?

60 × 3 + 660 ÷ 6 – 20 = 290
questions.solution:
Given:

60 × 3 + 660 ÷ 6 – 20 = 290

Calculation:

By option Method:

Option 1: exchange 6 and 660, × and ÷

⇒ 60 ÷ 3 + 6 x 660 – 20 = 290

⇒ 20 + 3960 - 20 = 290 

⇒ 3960 ≠ 290

This is not correct the equation.

Option 2: exchange 20 and 6, + and -

⇒ 60 × 3 - 660 ÷ 20 + 6 = 290

⇒ 180 - 33 + 6 = 290

⇒ 153  ≠ 290

This is not correct the equation.

Option 3: exchange 20 and 60, + and × 

⇒ 20 + 3 x 660 ÷ 6 – 60 = 290

⇒ 20 + 330 -60 = 290

⇒ 290 = 290

This is correct the equation.

Option 4: exchange 20 and 660, + and ÷

⇒ 60 × 3 ÷ 20 + 6 – 660 = 290

⇒ 9 + 6 - 660 = 290

⇒ -645 ≠ 290

This is not correct the equation.

Hence, 'Option 3' is the correct answer.

questions.question: Sharodi Saikia is an exponent of which Indian classical dance form?
questions.questionHtml: Sharodi Saikia is an exponent of which Indian classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sattriya .

Key Points

  • Her Sattriya dance is her specialty. 2015 saw Saikia win the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.
  • The dancer received the Bishnu Rabha Award from the Department of Cultural Affairs of the Government of Assam in 2022.
  • Guru Jatin Goswami, Guru Ghanakanta Bora, Manik and Bhabananda Barbayan, Moniram Dutta, and Dr. Bhupen Hazarika are a few of the top male Sattriya artists.
  • Sattriya dance's modern form is credited to Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardev, who created it to go with plays used for religious instruction.
  • The flute had been incorporated into the performance by the 15th century, and Sankardev had written music specifically for the dances.

Additional Information

  • In the 15th century, Srimanta Sankardev began a neo-Vaishnavite movement in Assam, which gave rise to the Sattriya sect.
  • He spread what is known as "ek sharan naama dharma" (chanting the name of one God devotedly).
  •  Ankiya bhaona and Ojapali dances, in which the lead singer sings, performs abhinaya, tells stories, and a group of dancer's dance as backup dancers while playing small cymbals, are both included in the corpus of Sattriya dances.
  • A significant component of Indian classical dance and music is ritualistic worship.
  • Assam's cultural legacy is inextricably linked to the more than 600-year-old Sattriya traditions and ritualistic practises found in mediaeval Vaishnavite monasteries, or sattras.
  • They offer a vivid view of Assamese culture by reflecting the ancient idioms of the land and society.
  • Kuchipudi: 
    • ​The dance-drama performance known as Kuchipudi has its origins in the Natya Shastra, an old Hindu scripture written in Sanskrit.
    • Like all significant Indian classical dances, it began as a religious art form associated with itinerant bards, temples, and spiritual beliefs.
    • Copper inscriptions from the 10th century and manuscripts like the Machupalli Kaifat from the 15th century both contain evidence of Kuchipudi's earlier existence.
    • According to Kuchipudi tradition, the contemporary form of Kuchipudi was established and systematized in the 17th century by the sanyasin Tirtha Narayana Yati and his student, an orphan named Siddhendra Yogi. 
  • Bharatanatyam: ​
    • ​Indian classical dance known as bharatanatyam has its roots in Tamil Nadu.
    • It reflects South Indian religious themes and spiritual ideals, primarily those of Shaivism and generally of Hinduism.
    • It is one of the eight Indian classical dance styles recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
  • Kathak: 
    • ​One of the eight primary styles of Indian classical dance is kathak.
    • It is an Uttar Pradesh classical dance style.
    • The storytellers or itinerant bards known as Kathakars in ancient northern India are often credited as the creators of Kathak.
    • The Vedic Sanskrit words Katha, which means "story," and Kathakar, which means "the one who tells a story "Or "to do with stories," are the roots of the word Kathak.

  • Sentence D is the last sentence as it begins with the noun 'Every school' and explains how each Samba school in Rio is required to follow their parade entries. Thus establishes a relation with the previous sentence.

The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

P. The division was usually based on temperature, which allows for different vegetation growth.

Q. Köppen’s map used different colors and shades to represent the different climate zones of the world.

R. Wladimir Köppen developed a climate classification system at the end of the 19th century.

S. The system divides the world into five climate zones.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e. "RSPQ." 
Key Points

  • In the abovementioned paragraph, there is a chronological sequence of the sentences.
  • Sentence R is the first sentence as it begins with the noun 'Wladimir Köppen'. It begins with introducing Wladimir Köppen and his work.
    It informs the reader that Köppen developed a climate classification system.
  • Sentence S is the second sentence as it begins with the noun 'The system' and explains the basic functioning of the climate classification system. It informs the reader that the system divides the world into five climate zones. Thus it establishes a relation with the previous sentence.
  • The only option that shows such an arrangement is Option 1.
  • Sentence P is the third sentence as it begins with the noun 'The division' and provides additional details about the system. It explains that the division is usually based on temperature, which affects vegetation growth.
  • Sentence Q is the last sentence as it begins with the noun 'Köppen’s map' and describes how Köppen's map represents the different climate zones of the world and uses different colours and shades to represent the various zones. Thus it establishes a relation with the previous sentence.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

The correct order is: 

R. Wladimir Köppen developed a climate classification system at the end of the 19th century.

S. The system divides the world into five climate zones.

P. The division was usually based on temperature, which allows for different vegetation growth.

Q. Köppen’s map used different colors and shades to represent the different climate zones of the world.

The correct answer is option 3) i.e. 'Many toys in the shop were broken by the child. Even the paintings were thrown by him.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in the active voice. We have to change the sentence into passive form. 
  • The given sentence is written in 'simple past tense.'
  • The structure of these kinds of sentences is:
    • Active Voice: Subject + V2 + Object.
    • Passive Voice:  Object + was/were + V3 + by (preposition) + Subject.
  • Let’s see another example:
    • Active voice: The gipsy girl opened the door.
    • Passive voice: The door was opened by the gipsy girl.
  • The subject of the given sentence is 'The child' and the object of the given sentence is 'many toys in the shop'. 
  • So, in the passive voice, the position of ‘subject’ and ‘object’ will be interchanged. 
  • Also here, 'broke' will be changed into 'were broken'.
  • The passive voice of the first part of the sentence is: Many toys in the shop were broken by the child.
  • Now, let's focus on the second part of the sentence.
  • The subject of the given sentence is 'He' and the object of the given sentence is 'the paintings'. 
  • So, in the passive voice, the position of ‘subject’ and ‘object’ will be interchanged. 
  • Also here, 'threw' will be changed into 'were thrown'.
  • 'he' will be changed into 'him'.
  • The passive voice of the first part of the sentence is: Even the paintings were thrown by him.

 

Correct Sentence: Many toys in the shop were broken by the child. Even the paintings were thrown by him.
